source.basis: Operator location page, structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

profile.reading: EdgeConneX Data Center, internally coded SAC01 per the operator own market page, sits in Rancho Cordova, California, part of the Sacramento metro area. The facility totals 28,500 square feet with 6,500 square feet of raised floor space for tenant racks. A notable feature disclosed on EdgeConneX own site is a rooftop solar installation developed in partnership with Madison Energy, a detail the company highlights as part of its sustainability approach at this location. No overall megawatt capacity figure, opening year, or named tenant is disclosed for the facility. One network-partnership announcement was found for this location, describing the Sacramento Internet Exchange deploying a node inside the EdgeConneX Sacramento facility, which names a connectivity partner rather than an anchor tenant. EdgeConneX is a US-based edge and build-to-suit data center operator founded in 2009 and headquartered in Herndon, Virginia, with regional headquarters in Amsterdam and Singapore. The company was acquired by EQT Infrastructure in 2020, and its board also includes a representative of Sixth Street, an investment firm, alongside EQT partners, though exact ownership percentages are not disclosed publicly. EdgeConneX describes its footprint today as more than 90 data centers across more than 60 markets in over 20 countries on four continents, and it operates a joint venture called AdaniConneX in India alongside a strategic investment in the China-based operator Chayora. The company model centers on build-to-suit and build-to-density facilities serving cloud, AI and high-performance computing, content-delivery, and network or ISP tenants. Rancho Cordova sits within the greater Sacramento metro area, a market that has grown as a secondary data center location for operators seeking proximity to the Bay Area without Silicon Valley own land and power constraints, and the rooftop solar feature EdgeConneX highlights here is consistent with a broader industry trend toward on-site renewable generation at smaller edge facilities.
profile.research_note: 28,500 sqft total / 6,500 sqft raised floor, rooftop solar with Madison Energy, and SAC01 designation confirmed via EdgeConneX own Sacramento market page. No MW, year-opened, or tenant disclosed.

reading.body:
EdgeConneX's Rancho Cordova facility publishes 28,500 square feet of technical space but no megawatt figure, making its AI infrastructure capacity impossible to assess from operator disclosures alone.

The facility holds six industry certifications spanning security, compliance, and sustainability. SOC 2 Type 2 and ISO 27001 certify the controls and systems required for sensitive workloads. HIPAA and PCI DSS narrow the use cases further to healthcare and payments. ENERGY STAR and UL 2799 Landfill Diversion address environmental performance. These certifications describe what the facility is qualified to host, not what it actually hosts or how much power it draws.

Among California's 103 mapped data centers, only five publish a megawatt figure on their operator spec pages. This facility is not among them. Without a disclosed power allocation, it cannot be ranked against peers, compared to California's constrained grid capacity, or assessed for its role in the state's AI infrastructure scaling. The absence of a megawatt figure is not a gap in available research, but a gap in what the operator chooses to disclose.
